reasoning_traces.think:
The core duality lies in the incompatibility of profit maximization and information elicitation. The stochastic approximation pricing mechanism (SA) models how bookmakers adjust prices based on incoming Kelly bets, while the fair-odds maximizer provides a closed-form solution for optimal pricing under idealized conditions. Regret bounds quantify the loss from not knowing the true distribution. These primitives form a dual framework: one optimizing for short-term gains (SA), another for long-term consistency (maximizer). The failure mode occurs when bettor beliefs are too noisy or non-stationary, breaking the convergence guarantees of SA and destabilizing the maximizer. The model assumes sequential arrival of bettors and perfect Kelly optimization, which may not reflect real-world heterogeneity.
